geometry_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass toward a split-wing/courtyard-capable configuration so the access edge can become publicly legible.
Keep the long axis aligned with the existing bar gesture.
Open a meaningful central gap to produce a public void rather than a cosmetic split.
Preserve a continuous base condition so the mass remains one hierarchy instead of fragmenting.
Introduce a courtyard anchored to the dominant mass to strengthen the public threshold.
Size the courtyard as a genuine program-supporting void.
Open the void toward the verified access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Bring the cantilever earlier so the ground-contact and overhang relationship reads as a clearer threshold at the access edge.
Add a dedicated access-side notch to create a legible public seam without destroying the dominant bent mass.
Align the notch with the verified access side in the program frame.
Keep the entry cut modest so the form remains one clear primary mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass across all four views, with the bend/cantilever producing a legible single gesture and acceptable hierarchy. It is not coherent in only one view and there is no visible collision across views. The form is somewhat boxy but the curved/stepped upper profile and the consistent sectional bend keep it from being a generic extrusion. Program fit passes for neighborhood living because the mass is compact, street-scaled, and not a wrong typology; however, the access edge response is weak: the thick blue frontage is met by a mostly sealed ground condition with no clearly carved public void or entry seam. That keeps void_publicness low and suggests a future courtyard/notch correction. Reference 1 supports the idea of a connected low-rise public composition with terrace/courtyard logic. Reference 2 supports compact neighborhood pavilion proportions and a modest active-edge posture, though it is less structurally comparable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More dispersed and campus-like than this compact street building; translate the courtyard/terrace logic, not the overall footprint.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise spread with a central/public open space and connected wings; the mass reads as one campus-like hierarchy rather than isolated blocks.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much flatter and more pavilion-like than the candidate; do not copy the detached canopy-heavy composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact pavilion massing with a clear active edge and a modest service/vertical accent; good for a neighborhood-scale ground response.

warnings: Public threshold on the verified access edge is under-articulated; the mass should carve or notch the frontage rather than simply occupy the parcel.
The proposal is coherent but still reads somewhat sealed at the ground, so the void/public relation needs strengthening.
Top view suggests a bent bar, but the access-side opening is not yet fully legible.
